channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Explains 4% Mortgage Program Without Down Payment
item.description: Kyrgyz citizens can now obtain housing through a state mortgage program at 4% annual interest without a down payment, announced President Sadyr Japarov. He clarified that recipients can move in and make monthly payments over 25 years. A separate program exists for those who can afford a 50% down payment.

item.title: Manas and Osh Airports to Expand Voice Communication Recording System for 13.6 Million Som
item.description: Kyrgyzavia Navigation plans to expand the Neptuno voice recording system at Manas and Osh airports for 13.6 million som. The upgrade will add 41 analog communication channels, aiming to ensure automatic recording, centralized control, and archiving of air traffic controller communications.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Responds to Concerns Over 'Junda' Oil Refinery's Environmental Impact
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov addressed residents' concerns about the environmental impact of the 'Junda' oil refinery in Kara-Balta. Residents reported health issues they attribute to the plant. Japarov emphasized the need for industrial development, stating that closing factories is not an option, but did not rule out relocating residents if health problems are proven.

item.title: Seven New Production Facilities Launched in Kara-Balta Over Five Years, Creating 560 Jobs
item.description: Over the past five years, Kara-Balta has seen the launch of seven new production facilities, creating 560 jobs. This development includes enterprises in metallurgy, gold bar production, and textiles. Additionally, 36 social facilities were built, and road infrastructure was improved. Investment was also attracted to the mining sector in the neighboring region.

item.title: Sons-in-Law of Influential Women in Central Asia Control Significant Assets
item.description: In Central Asian nations, the status of a president's son-in-law grants access to political influence and control over economic sectors, often ensuring immunity. However, this position is precarious, depending entirely on the father-in-law. The article details how sons-in-law can lose assets and influence if they fall out of favor or during power transitions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Presidential Election: Preliminary Voter Lists Include 4.4 Million Citizens
item.description: Preliminary voter lists for the presidential election in Kyrgyzstan now include 4,467,040 citizens, according to the Central Election Commission. The lists will be posted at 2,492 polling stations nationwide until November 18 and are also available on the tizme.gov.kg portal. Citizens can verify their inclusion until January 12, 2027.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Building Second Tunnel at Too-Ashu Pass
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is exploring the possibility of constructing a second, alternative tunnel at a lower elevation on the Too-Ashu pass. President Sadyr Japarov announced this, stating it could reduce vehicle traffic. The project is considered prospective, with no specific timelines or costs yet revealed.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Flour Exports Surge, Afghanistan and Kyrgyzstan Top Buyers
item.description: Kazakhstan's flour production and exports have increased significantly. From January to August 2026, exports reached 1.4 million tons, valued at $400 million. Afghanistan remains the largest buyer, with 874,300 tons, followed by Kyrgyzstan, which maintained its purchase volume.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Reveals Electricity Cost and Subsidy Details
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov stated that the cost of electricity in Kyrgyzstan is 3.25 soms per kilowatt-hour, while citizens pay only 1.64 soms. He explained that the state covers the difference using the republican budget. Japarov urged timely payments, noting that further consumer benefits may be considered after overcoming the energy crisis.

item.title: Trump: No Reason for Escalated Conflict with Iran, Expects Negotiation
item.description: Former US President Donald Trump stated there is no reason for the US to escalate military conflict with Iran and expects Tehran to eventually negotiate a deal. He affirmed that while the US retains the capability to strike targets, he does not see a current need for such operations, claiming Iran has already lost the war and is ready for an agreement.

item.title: Do the Taliban Read History? Examining Their Governance Approach
item.description: The author questions whether the Taliban read history, noting their governance relies heavily on coercion, similar to their interpretation of early Islamic history. This selective reading prevents them from understanding modern governance in advanced nations, where force is not the sole tool. Their approach lacks broader historical perspective.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Digitalizes Civil Aviation Management System
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is continuing efforts to implement the EMPIC-EAP system, aimed at digitizing regulatory processes in civil aviation. Practical seminars and training sessions were held by the Civil Aviation State Agency with EMPIC representatives. The focus was on the capabilities and implementation of the Personnel Licensing (PEL) module for aviation personnel.

item.title: Camera Traps Installed in Zorkul Reserve for Wildlife Monitoring
item.description: Automatic camera traps have been installed in the Zorkul State Nature Reserve to enhance scientific monitoring of wild animals during the winter period. Placed along migration routes and gathering spots, the cameras will help specialists study species composition, estimate populations, and track seasonal movements to aid conservation efforts.

item.title: New Apple Juice Concentrate Plant Opens in Jalal-Abad Region
item.description: A new apple juice concentrate plant, owned by "Global Eco Green" LLC, has been launched in the Alabuka district of the Jalal-Abad region. The facility can process up to 500 tons of apple concentrate daily and is expected to create up to 100 new jobs. The plant aims to help farmers sell their produce and promote local processing.

item.title: Kazakh Citizen Alleges Fraud in Quarry Deal, Claims Connection to Kyrgyz President's Relative
item.description: A Kazakh national, Alizhi Afarov, has complained to Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov, claiming he was defrauded of over $200,000 in a quarry purchase near Kant. Afarov stated one suspect introduced himself as Azamat Japarov, a relative of the president, though this was later found to be untrue. He suspects organized crime involvement.

item.title: New Enterprises Drive Job Creation in Tajikistan, Report Finds
item.description: Newly established enterprises accounted for approximately 60% of job creation in Tajikistan, according to a report by the Eurasian Development Fund. The study, covering Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Armenia, highlights significant job growth in hospitality and manufacturing sectors. Researchers advise caution due to potential low-base effects.

item.title: New Rescue System Tested in Almaty Mountains for Tourist Safety
item.description: A new AG Tag device, enabling tourists to call for help even without mobile signal or internet, is being tested in the Almaty mountains. The device uses satellite positioning to transmit coordinates via radio to rescuers. A simple SOS button press sends a signal visible on the rescue service's electronic map, updating every two seconds. The system can transmit signals up to 15 kilometers.

item.title: Iran's Top Diplomat Warns US: Choose Peace Deal or Continued Conflict
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has told the White House that the US must choose between accepting Iran's demands for peace or continuing the war, following the US midterm elections. Araghchi stated that Iran's proposal remains on the table and that Washington could see positive results by accepting its terms, including an end to hostilities. He warned that Iran's military forces are prepared to respond if the US chooses conflict.

item.title: Taliban Supporters' Clerics to Gather at Kabul University Amid Student Evictions
item.description: Sources report that students at Kabul University have been evicted from dormitories for nearly a week. Taliban officials have ordered the evictions to allow for renovations and to accommodate clerics for a gathering. This displacement occurs as students approach final exams, causing significant difficulties.

item.title: Pakistan's Bank Alfalah Ceases Operations in Afghanistan After 20 Years
item.description: Pakistan's Bank Alfalah, the largest foreign bank in Afghanistan, has ceased operations after 20 years. The bank transferred its business, assets, and liabilities to the local Ghazanfar Bank. This marks the exit of a significant foreign financial institution from the Afghan market.

item.title: President Orders Resolution of Resident's Housing Dispute in Tokmok
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has instructed the Ministry of Construction to review the case of a Tokmok resident who paid for an apartment in 2022 but has not yet received it. The resident reported the issue during a meeting with the president, stating they paid in full but were informed by the GKNB that the apartment was being taken. The construction minister has pledged to investigate the matter.

item.title: Train Collision in Egypt Kills Four and Injures 88
item.description: A collision between two passenger trains south of Cairo has resulted in at least four deaths and 88 injuries. Several carriages derailed following the incident. Egypt's state railway authority reported that a train from Giza collided with the rear of another train heading to Aswan. An investigation has been ordered.

item.title: Two Passenger Trains Collide in Egypt, Resulting in Fatalities
item.description: Four people were killed and at least 88 injured when two passenger trains collided in Egypt's El-Ayat district on November 8. Investigators are considering two main theories: a railway signaling failure or a possible violation of traffic rules by the driver. The Ministry of Transport stated train No. 134 hit the rear of train No. 2010.

item.title: Krakow Shooting Officially Classified as Terrorism
item.description: Polish prosecutors have officially classified the mass shooting in Krakow's city center as a terrorist act. The investigation combines the attack with the deaths of the suspect's family members. Evidence suggests a single perpetrator with radical views.

item.title: Millions of Afghans Face Healthcare Crisis as Humanitarian Aid Declines
item.description: The UN reports that up to 700 healthcare facilities in Afghanistan may close or face severe financial strain by the end of 2026 due to declining humanitarian aid. This reduction in support makes service delivery more difficult and exacerbates the population's basic needs. Local residents in provinces like Baghlan are already complaining about long distances to reach functional clinics.

item.title: Unexploded Ordnance Explosion Kills 25-Year-Old Man in Ghazni Province
item.description: A 25-year-old man, identified as Mohammad Karim, was killed by an explosion involving unexploded ordnance in the Mir Khan village of Qarabagh district, Ghazni province. The incident occurred after children brought scrap metal, including the ordnance, into their home. This follows a similar fatal incident in the Ab Band district of the same province.

item.title: Uzbekistan Boosts Labor Migration Support and International Pension Agreements
item.description: Uzbekistan is enhancing support for labor migrants, aiming to increase remittances while reducing the number of citizens working abroad. The government will incentivize private agencies for placing migrants in high-paying jobs and create a special registry. Efforts are underway to secure international agreements, particularly with Russia, South Korea, and Japan, to ensure migrants' pension rights are recognized upon return.

item.title: Kabul Residents Report Severe Power Outages Ahead of Winter
item.description: Kabul residents are experiencing severe electricity shortages, with only one to two hours of power per day. The situation worsens as winter approaches, despite the need for electricity year-round. Officials from the state-run power company have acknowledged rationing but did not respond to recent complaints.

item.title: European Nations to Join Russia-US-Ukraine Talks in Abu Dhabi, French Minister Says
item.description: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot announced that European countries, including France, will participate in trilateral talks between Russia, the United States, and Ukraine. These negotiations are scheduled to take place in Abu Dhabi. The specific European representatives were not disclosed.

item.title: Ukraine President Reports Over 600,000 Without Power After Russian Attacks
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that over 600,000 people in Dnipro and surrounding areas lost electricity due to Russian attacks on energy infrastructure. Rescue operations continue for those affected by an earlier strike. Power outages also reported in Kharkiv and heating issues in Zhytomyr.

item.title: Over 900 Square Kilometers of Afghanistan Contaminated by Unexploded Ordnance
item.description: Afghanistan's Disaster Management Preparedness Authority reports that 901 square kilometers of the country are contaminated with unexploded ordnance. These munitions, remnants of past conflicts, continue to pose a threat to citizens, causing casualties annually. International organizations are working to clear these areas.

item.title: Russian Attacks on Ukraine's Power Facilities Leave 600,000 Without Electricity
item.description: Russian attacks on Ukraine's power infrastructure on Sunday left approximately 600,000 residents in eastern regions without electricity. President Zelensky accused Russia of attempting to plunge Ukraine into darkness ahead of upcoming talks in Abu Dhabi.

item.title: Taliban Army Chief Claims Pakistan Supports Anti-Taliban Opposition Groups
item.description: Taliban army chief Fasihuddin Fitrat claimed that anti-Taliban armed opposition groups are not Afghan and receive support from Pakistan. He alleged foreign powers helped create these groups, which he called 'rebels,' after the U.S. withdrawal.

item.title: Kazakhstan Upgrades Emergency Services with New Fire Station and Safety Complex
item.description: Two new safety infrastructure facilities have opened in Kazakhstan's Almaty region: a renovated fire station in Kонаев and a multi-functional "Aul Zhany" post in the Ili district. Both are equipped with modern technology and essential equipment, enhancing emergency response capabilities.

item.title: Turkey Detains 63 Afghan Migrants in Border Province of Hakkari
item.description: Turkish police have detained 63 Afghan migrants in the border province of Hakkari. The migrants were apprehended attempting to enter Turkey illegally. Authorities also arrested an individual suspected of smuggling them. Turkey continues operations to prevent illegal migration.

item.title: Afghanistan and Uzbekistan Sign 18 Trade Agreements Worth Over $150 Million
item.description: Businessmen from Afghanistan and Uzbekistan have signed 18 trade agreements valued at over $150 million. The deals cover food products, clothing, construction materials, and import-export sectors. This marks a significant step in expanding economic cooperation between the two nations.

item.title: Kazakh President Expresses Condolences to Polish President After Krakow Shooting
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev sent a telegram of condolences to Polish President Karol Nawrocki following the shooting incident in Krakow. The head of state strongly condemned the act of violence and expressed solidarity with the Polish people, wishing a speedy recovery to the injured.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Fourth-Class Wheat Surpasses Third-Class in Price
item.description: A paradoxical situation has emerged in Kazakhstan's domestic market, where fourth-class wheat is now priced higher than the more quality third-class. Experts attribute this to a high-quality harvest this season, resulting in a scarcity of lower-class wheat, which is in demand for feed production.

item.title: UNICEF Reports Sharp Increase in Acute Malnutrition Among Afghan Children
item.description: UNICEF data indicates a significant rise in acute malnutrition among young children in Afghanistan. Rates climbed to 12% in Q3 2026, up from 9.3% in the previous quarter and 11% a year prior. Critical levels were observed in 16 of the country's 34 provinces.

item.title: Kazakh Citizen Claims He Was Defrauded by Someone Posing as President Japarov's Relative
item.description: A Kazakh citizen, Alidzhi Afarov, reported to President Sadyr Japarov that he was defrauded of $200,000 by an individual claiming to be the president's relative. Afarov stated he purchased a quarry, but organized crime members allegedly seized the property through deception. The president has ordered an investigation.
